reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and, consistent with that, no redline or comment was proposed — the rendered paragraph is unchanged from the original.

The cited § (h) supports compliance: it permits either Party (including the Customer, AP) to assign without consent to an affiliate, a purchaser of substantially all relevant assets, or a successor by merger/stock sale/consolidation, with all other assignments subject to consent that may not be unreasonably withheld. That satisfies the fallback (mutual successor assignment plus reasonable-consent standard) and includes the M&A carve-out the rule requires.
No change-of-control trigger exists, so the Vendor has no termination or re-pricing right on a Customer change of control; walk-away territory is not implicated.

Shortfalls versus the preferred position (symmetrical rather than one-way consent restriction; no express bar on assignment to a Customer competitor) are minor sub-elements correctly noted in the rationale rather than redlined.
Deterministic check confirming the successor/affiliate carve-out passes, and the analysis correctly distinguishes the § 2 licence-scope 'non-transferable' language from the assignment provision.
